summary: The iX2 is the coupe-roofed version of BMW's iX1 electric small SUV, sharing its 230kW dual-motor drivetrain and 64.8kWh usable pack but trading a little rear headroom for a sleeker tail and a slightly bigger 525-litre boot. Australian reviewers consistently rate the powertrain, cabin quality and body control highly while calling out the 395km ADR range as short for the money, and a ride that is firmer than the iX1's on the standard 19-inch M wheels. A $7,700 price cut in March 2026 dropped it to $79,900 and simultaneously deleted the front-drive eDrive20, so the range is now a single dual-motor grade.
pros: 230kW/494Nm dual-motor all-wheel drive gets it to 100km/h in 5.6 seconds, quicker than a Volvo EX40 Twin Motor and most of the segment
525-litre boot is roughly 35L larger than the iX1's despite the coupe roofline, expanding to 1400L
$7,700 cut in March 2026 brought it to $79,900 before on-roads, only $2,000 above the iX1 xDrive30 and now below the LCT threshold for fuel-efficient vehicles
Adaptive M suspension and a boost paddle give it genuinely engaging body control that reviewers rank above the Mercedes-Benz EQA
1200kg braked towing capacity with the optional bar, which several small electric SUVs cannot match
cons: 395km ADR range is short for an $80k EV — CarExpert measured 19.1kWh/100km against the 18.5kWh/100km claim, implying closer to 350km in mixed driving
Firmer, busier ride than the iX1, and reviewers report the 20-inch wheel option makes it noticeably worse over sharp bumps
Sloping roofline costs rear headroom, and the raised battery floor leaves taller adults sitting knees-up
Now a one-grade range — the cheaper front-drive eDrive20 was discontinued in Australia in 2026, so there is no lower entry point
Buyers of the pre-cut $87,600 car lost close to 9 per cent of list overnight, which weighs on used values
